name: game-music-emu
why: Plays chiptune music from dozens of retro game sound chips, turning old console files back into audio.

brief.what_it_is: Game_Music_Emu is a C library, with a demo and an SDL player, that emulates the sound hardware of classic game consoles and computers so their music files can be played back as audio. It takes music data files in formats such as NSF/NSFE, SPC, VGM/VGZ, GBS, HES, KSS, GYM, SAP and AY and produces PCM audio samples. The bundled demo, basics.c, records an NSF file to a WAV file (out.wav). The README lists about ten format families, not dozens of chips as the scout note suggests.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as Blargg's video game music emulation library, which lets audio applications add playback support for the music of many classic video game consoles. Its stated emphasis is making the library very easy to use.
brief.how_it_works: Each supported system has its own emulator (CPU plus sound chip core), and all of them share one common C interface. The library can read music data from a file, memory, or a custom reader, and can read track information without loading the full emulator. It resamples output to an adjustable sample rate and supports end-of-track fading, silence detection, stereo echo, tempo changes, muting of individual voices, and M3U playlists.

brief.install_notes: No brew-specific notes were in the scout data. From the README: building needs CMake 3.3 or later, or you can compile demo/basics.c, demo/Wave_Writer.cpp and all files in gme/ directly. The demo needs test.nsf in the same directory to produce out.wav. The optional player in player/ requires the SDL library. No accounts or runtimes are mentioned.
brief.standout: A single uniform C API covers many unrelated sound chips, and track metadata can be read without running the emulator. It is a library for other players to embed, and it has been used in players on Windows, Linux, macOS, MorphOS, Xbox, PSP, GP2X and Nintendo DS.
brief.status: Probably maintained, though the evidence is partial. The README names two current maintainers (Vitaly Novichkov and Michael Pyne), the repo shows 446 commits, 197 stars, and CI workflows under .github/workflows, and the README is at version 0.6.6. The page I read did not show a last-commit date or release date, so this is not confirmed.
brief.caveats: The license is LGPL-2.1, but the README says that using the MAME YM2612 emulator changes the library's license to GPL v2.0 or later. KSS does not support FM sound. The project is a library rather than a finished player, and the demo only records to WAV. The player needs SDL. The scout note's 'dozens of chips' overstates what the README lists.
